### Page 1

•Broad-base 2Q, cost-capped margin. Mgmt. reiterated that 2Q26 growth 
was broad-based across every product line, end market and region, not a 
single AI pocket. GPM was slightly below Street, as raw material cost 
inflation offset part of the pricing and mix improvement. Internal 
manufacturing efficiency projects are underway to absorb it in the future.
•Jul price hike hits spot and direct. The Jul price adjustment covers spot 
prices and direct customers, vs. earlier rounds limited to contract 
customers, and spans c.50% of revenue including MLCC, tantalum and 
other capacitors. Spot pricing flows through immediately rather than at 
renewal, so mgmt. expects ASP and revenue effects shortly, with margin 
impact far more visible in 2H. Mgmt. also sees no sign of demand slowing 
down in the near-term.
•Tantalum now the largest line. AI is not an MLCC-only story for passive 
components. Tantalum grew fastest of any line in 2Q, suits AI power 
management, and has over taken magnetics to become Yageo's largest 
product line. MLCC also grew well and should keep growing in coming 
quarters. AI revenue is now 16% of total revenue, spread across tantalums, 
MLCCs, resistors and inductors rather than single product.
•65 sites, dual-region by product. Every product is manufactured in at least 
two regions, giving customers flexibility against tariff and geopolitical risks. 
Mgmt. believe the existing 65 facilities are flexible in adding new lines at a 
fast pace whenever shortages appear, saving customers 1-2 years vs. 
building from greenfield. The company also planned the capacity expansion 
ahead of demand.

### Page 2

Yageo (2327.TW)
04 September 2026 Citi Research
2
•YFIII and overseas MLCC bases. YFIII in Kaohsiung, commissioned in 2024, is Yageo's largest MLCC fab and still has
space for additional MLCC lines, with AI-specific equipment arriving monthly since last year. Outside Taiwan, Yageo
has been opening new lines within existing facilities in Mexico and China, leaving it able to absorb incremental AI
orders without a new building cycle.
•Lead times extend, LTA interest rises. Lead time of most of the products has lengthened vs. 1H26. Tantalum is the

tightest, followed by MLCC and resistors. Mgmt. indicated all AI-related lines are extremely tight, and more
customers are now approaching Yageo to sign LTAs.
•NP0 leadership on the power side. Yageo estimates a meaningful share (at least 30-40%) of NP0 high-voltage
MLCC, based on the internal assessment. Built on EV and industrial experience, NP0 fits AI's high-voltage, high-
temp duty and sits on the DC power side, while high-cap MLCC serves the near-chip stage. Yageo ships direct to

leading power supply players and is invited as first batch of design partners.
•Low-to-high conversion only partial. Converting low-end MLCC capacity to high-end is only partially possible.
High-spec MLCC stores more capacitance through higher layer counts, requiring advanced stackers rather than
conventional equipment. Yageo can optimize and redeploy some existing tooling, but not fully substitute, which is
why it is committing capex to new AI production line instead of relying on conversion.

Yageo
Valuation
We set our target price at NT$1,450, based on 35x average 2027E-28E earnings. We value Yageo based on PE as we believe the
company’s earnings performance and industry dynamics would be the key focuses of the market. Our target multiple of 35x is
at the higher end of the trading range since 2022. During this period the company has gone through the cycles, successfully
integrated the acquired business to enhance its product offerings, and started to deliver stable margins and earnings.

Risks
Key downside risks to our target price and rating include: 1) slower-than-expected demand recovery; 2) intensified peer and
pricing competition; 3) execution risks associated with M&A integration and synergies; and 4) FX and interest rate fluctuations.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

Strong CPO ramp priced ahead of qualification
The re-rating has outpaced qualification progress; downgrade from Buy to Sell
Largan shares have risen 242% since April on optimism around its CPO FAU progress.
While we stay constructive on Largan's CPO prospects, we believe the market is pricing
in confidence ahead of still-early qualification progress, particularly given a crowded
competitive field. Largan only starts its sample line late Q3, integrating its Prism Micro

Lens Array and Fiber Array with AOET's V-groove and Corning's fiber. We expect  several
quarters to improve yields, gain integrator acceptance (Corning, Senko, AuthenX) and
convert its initial production-oriented FA program into volume while competing against
incumbent TFC and vertically integrated rivals incl. Coherent. We downgrade our rating
from Buy to Sell with CPO still at an early stage and the stock now 35x 2027 vs. LT 13-
18x range well above our sum-of-the-parts NT$5,000 PT based on 15x smartphone lens

+ 50x CPO base case for 40% share  (upper end of optical peers  at 14-72x).
Still a range of outcomes for CPO solution traction
Largan's approach pairs V-groove with PMLA to shape the optical light from the PIC into
the fiber at high accuracy with automated assembly. Feedback is positive on Largan's
precision and track record for volume production/yield improvement (now still low) and
1 FA design in an FAU. A risk is Largan targeting the Gen 3 optics should take until 2028

and also competes with incumbent TFC which is already designed-in for 2026-27 and
other FAU vendors like Coherent that can vertically integrate or use meta lens not
requiring Largan's initial V-groove approach. Largan's push toward a complete solution
may also conflict with integration partners.
Core smartphone lens tracking behind amid memory headwinds
We also see risk on near-term results with Q326 sales tracking light. Aug sales were NT
$5bn, +3% MoM, -16% YoY, taking QTD revenue to NT$10.1bn, 53% of UBSe/Street

Q326. Sept would need to grow +73% MoM to meet UBSe/Street +36-38% QoQ vs.
normal seasonal +8% MoM. We expect flattish builds at best for its flagship customer
(80% of sales) needing to raise price to pass on memory costs +US$200-300 YoY albeit
some support from high-end introducing variable-aperture lens, while foldable lens
specs remain similar. Factoring muted smartphone growth but healthy margins, we view
a mid-teens multiple appropriate for this business, in line with its historical range.

Stock prices in our upside case ahead of traction; risk-reward skews negative
We maintain basic '26E/27E EPS at NT$190/NT$214 and NT$5,000 SOTP PT based on 1)
15x smartphone lens (NT$3,270) + 2) 50x CPO base case EPS of NT$35 for NT$1,730
(40% share, 100k switches/7.2mn FAUs, US$150/FAU, US$1.1bn TAM), high-end of
peers due to its premium ~40-45% OpM. We view risk/reward skewed negative with
downside to NT$2,500 on limited CPO success and softer smartphones, base case NT

$5,000 for CPO traction, and upside 22% if the stock is bid to our upside case NT$9,000
based on top-end 70x P/E on CPO earnings at 60% share of a higher US$1.58bn TAM.

Thesis Map     UBS                    Research     THESIS MAP a guide to our thinking and what´s where in this report
Q: Could Largan's CPO products contribute meaningful revenue in a few years?
We stay constructive but the company still has hurdles to clear in a crowded space. Its scale and track
record in high-end smartphone lens gives it an opportunity supplying key components of the CPO

FAU assembly, traditional strength in precision lens micro assemblies, alignment accuracy, in-house
tooling and automation that could give it a differentiated solution. Our feedback at Semicon Taiwan
suggests the company is still early in qualification, with its sample production line for customer
evaluation readied in late September and still requiring work with a system integrator and
qualification with the fabless customer and ODMs.  We still see a year to move from sampling to

design-in but if successful timed to meet expected market acceleration in 2028-29.
Q: Will there be further technology upgrades driving the lens cycle in the coming years?
We expect spec upgrades for Largan's core lens business to come in H226 from variable aperture
shipments for the iPhone 18 (which Genius does not currently participate though may enter over
time, as seen with periscope lenses). Key offset though is weaker sales with Q3 tracking light and

suggesting a softer build due to memory headwinds. Further upside could come from broader
adoption of 48MP modules in future iPhone models. Looking longer term, Apple is reportedly
exploring 200MP periscope lens and adjacent opportunities to penetrate physical AI categories with
precision lens including robotics, autonomous systems and AR/VR devices.
We downgrade our rating on Largan from Buy to Sell as we view the market expectations as now
pricing in a bullish scenario for strong market traction with the company still at an early stage of

qualification, still needing to improve its process and yields, and competing in a crowded space also
against an existing incumbent. We expect several quarters to improve current low yields, gain
acceptance from solution integrators (Corning, Senko, AuthenX) and secure design-ins by the AI GPU
fabless company and its ODM partners against incumbent TFC and other rivals. We downgrade
Largan from Buy to Sell with CPO still at an early stage and the stock now 35x 2027 vs. LT 13-18x

range and well above our sum-of-the-parts NT$5,000 price target based on 15x smartphone lens +
50x CPO base case for40% share  (upper-end of optical peer range of 14-72x).
Largan has demonstrated its samples with partners at Computex and Semicon Taiwan and cited its
goals to ramp CPO as its next opportunity. The company is still early in qualifications with a sample
automated line in the coming months followed by design-in engagement with system integrators,

ODMs and the fabless customer to target design-in on 3rd gen CPO solutions in 2028. For
smartphone lens, its top customer had a strong iPhone 17 cycle although acknowledged it would
have to raise price to pass on higher memory costs which could dampen growth. Sales QTD are
tracking slightly light as Largan also competes with 2nd source Genius. Our supply chain checks and
management commentary points to introduction of higher value variable aperture lens in H226.

Largan is currently trading above the high end of its historical range at 39x/35x our 2026E/27E EPS vs.
a long-term range of 13-18x forward consensus earning, pricing in success penetrating the CPO
component market ahead of the earnings stream which would only start late in 2027 into 2028. We
note optical component peers trade at 14-72x with an average of ~38x 2027E P/E (Genius at 25x
2027 P/E). We maintain our SOTP valuation with our price target at NT$5000 based on 1) 15x

smartphone lens (NT$3,270) + 2) 50x CPO base case EPS of NT$35 for NT$1,730 (40% share, 100k
switches/7.2mn FAUs, US$150/FAU, US$1.1bn TAM), high-end of peers due to its premium ~40-
45% OpM. We view the stock at NT$7,400 now pricing in CPO traction on a 50x multiple of our
upside NT$76 case based on 60% share of an upside US$1.6bn opportunity.

Largan Precision UBS Research
commentary
Largan shares have risen 242% since 1 April on optimism around its CPO fiber array unit
(FAU) progress. While we stay constructive post our feedback at Semicon Taiwan on
Largan's ability to develop CPO solutions, we now believe the market is pricing in a level
of confidence that has run well ahead of qualification progress which is still early and
competing in a crowded field. Largan will only start its sample line in late Q3 integrating

its Prism Micro Lens Array and Fiber Array, AOET's V-groove and Corning's glass fiber.
From there, we expect several quarters to improve current low yields, gain acceptance
from solution integrators (Corning, Senko, AuthenX) and secure design-ins by the AI
GPU fabless company and its ODM partners against incumbent TFC and rivals including
Coherent with own lens/FAU. The company did note on its Q226 call that it had secured
one mass production commitment for its fiber array to an FAU maker that could ramp by

H227 although early to conclude the magnitude of this engagement or end customer
design-in, with the other customers still at proof-of-concept phase.
We downgrade our rating on Largan from Buy to Sell with CPO still at an early stage and
the stock now 35x 2027 vs. LT 13-18x range and well above our sum-of-the-parts NT
$5,000 price target based on 15x smartphone lens + 50x CPO base case for 40% share
(upper-end of optical component peers trading at a  range of 14-72x).

Still a range of outcomes for CPO solution traction
Largan's approach pairs V-groove with PMLA to shape the optical light from the PIC into
the fiber at high accuracy with automated assembly. Feedback is positive on Largan's
precision and track record for volume production/yield improvement (now still low). A
risk is Largan targeting the Gen 3 optics should take until 2028 and also competes with

incumbent TFC which is already designed-in for 2026-27 and other FAU vendors like
Coherent that can vertically integrate or use meta lens not requiring Largan's initial V-
groove approach. Largan's business model may also conflict with integration partners as
it also attempts to build toward a complete solution.
We estimate Largan's Total Addressable Market in a downside case is US$270mn if it
only supplies sub-components into a market that continues to push out CPO due to

reliability concerns relative to pluggables and NPO/XPO options, US$1.08bn in a base
case with 100k switches and 72 FAUs per switch at US$150 ASP , and US$1.6bn in an
upside case with 125k switches, 72 FAUs per switch and US$175 ASP .  For Largan, we
estimate downside case 10% share yields NT$810mn sales and NT$2.20 EPS, base case
40% share, NT$13.0bn sales and NT$35 EPS, and upside case 60% share, NT$28.4bn
sales and NT$76 EPS.
Although we are optimistic on the market opportunity scaling up and Largan's

competencies and progress developing these solutions, Largan's traction is not yet
certain and it will compete in a crowded landscape. We believe Himax is already
supplying wafer level optics for the collimator function with FOCI (3363.TWO) and TFC
(300394.SZ) already has demonstrated capability and design-in on the FAU and lens
assembly. Others that could vertically integrate include Coherent, Senko, Corning and
Sumitomo, and we also note Genius sending samples and Sunny Optical's intention to

develop for this market.

UPSIDE (NT$9,000): Our upside valuation of NT$3,655 is based on  its average P/E of 16x
off our 2027 upside case EPS of NT$235. We factor in faster than expected
CPO progress to deliver upside EPS of NT$76 and 70x P/E at the high end of optical peers
trading at 14-72x 2027E P/E to an implied valuation of NT$5,345, and  total share price at
NT$9,000.
BASE (NT$5,000):  Our price target for its smartphone business is NT$3,270, with a 15x
2027 P/E applied on its base case EPS of NT$214 slightly below the long-term average of

its historical P/E band to reflect the macro uncertainty. Paired with our base scenario of its
CPO business at NT$35 EPS and 50x P/E, we arrive at an implied valuation of NT$1,730,
and Largan's aggregate PT  at NT$5,000.
DOWNSIDE (NT$2,500):   Downside valuation at NT$2,392, based on low-end of its
range 13x 2027 P/E. We take into consideration slower adoption of FAUs at its downside
EPS of NT$2 and the same 50x P/E to  an implied valuation of NT$108 for

CPO contribution, and Largan's total share price at NT$2,500.

Company Description
Founded in 1987, Largan Precision (Largan) is one of the world's leading manufacturers of
lenses used in cameras and IT products. It specialises in plastic/hybrid lenses and, to a lesser
extent, glass lenses and modules. In 2022, 20MP+ camera lenses were 10-20% of Largan's

shipment mix, 10MP lenses were 50-60%, 8MP lenses were 0-10% and other lenses were
30-40%.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
Our price target is based on SOTP valuation on the CPO opportunity and traditional lens
business.
We think Largan's downside risks include: 1) ongoing pricing pressure from smartphone OEM
clients and increasingly intense competition among lens suppliers; and 2) a slower-than-
expected smartphone demand recovery in China, and 3) CPO commercial success below the

market's elevated expectations.
We believe the key upside risk is a faster-than-expected CPO qualification process at Largan.
In addition, if the company demonstrates exceptionally efficient and highly accurate
automation capabilities, it could support greater market share gains within the industry than
we currently anticipate.

WinWay Technology
Valuation
We value WinWay using a PE-based approach that factors in earnings momentum and likely expansion of its addressable
market. Our target price of NT$11,500 is derived from applying c.41x to 2H27E-1H28E EPS, higher than the upper end of its
long-term PE range, which we believe is justified given the company's entrenched position in the high-end AI GPU testing
supply chain, rising contribution from coaxial socket and SLT solutions, and the increasing value of test content per module.

With these structural drivers in place, and as we believe the market is starting to value it as an AI/HPC play (rather than a
consumer electronics stock), we expect the multiple to hold at a premium relative to its historical averages.
Risks
Our quant rating system rates the WinWay stock High Risk based on its historical volatility.
Key downside risks that could impede the stock from reaching our target price and our earnings forecasts include: 1) client and

sector concentration – specifically any delays in US AI GPU product roadmap could impact the business outlook for WinWay; 2)
intensifying competition in coaxial and hypersockets from global peers; 3) faster-than-expected testing algorithm
optimization, which could shorten testing durations and reduce the anticipated hardware demand multiplier; and 4) delay of
MEMS Phase 2 mass production.

Guide to Citi Research Fundamental Research Investment Ratings:
Citi Research stock recommendations include an investment rating and an optional risk rating to highlight high risk stocks.

Risk rating takes into account both price volatility and fundamental criteria. Stocks will either have no risk rating or a High risk
rating assigned.
Investment Ratings: Citi Research investment ratings are Buy, Neutral and Sell. Our ratings are a function of analyst
expectations of expected total return ("ETR") and risk. ETR is the sum of the forecast price appreciation (or depreciation) plus
the dividend yield for a stock within the next 12 months.  The target price is based on a 12 month time horizon. The Investment

rating definitions are: Buy (1) ETR of 15% or more or 25% or more for High risk stocks; and Sell (3) for negative ETR. Any covered
stock not assigned a Buy or a Sell is a Neutral (2). For stocks rated Neutral (2), if an analyst believes that there are insufficient
valuation drivers and/or investment catalysts to derive a positive or negative investment view, they may elect with the approval
of Citi Research management not to assign a target price and, thus, not derive an ETR. Citi Research may suspend its rating

and target price and assign “Rating Suspended” status for regulatory and/or internal policy reasons. Citi Research may also
suspend its rating and target price and assign "Under Review" status for other exceptional circumstances (e.g. lack of
information critical to the analyst's thesis, trading suspension) affecting the company and/or trading in the company's
securities. In both such situations, the rating and target price will show as “—“ and “-“ respectively in the rating history price

chart. Prior to 11 April 2022 Citi Research assigned “Under Review” status to both situations and prior to 11 Nov 2020 only in
exceptional circumstances. As soon as practically possible, the analyst will publish a note re-establishing a rating and
investment thesis. Investment ratings are determined by the ranges described above at the time of initiation of coverage, a
change in investment and/or risk rating, or a change in target price (subject to limited management discretion). At times, the

expected total returns may fall outside of these ranges because of market price movements and/or other short-term volatility
or trading patterns. Such interim deviations will be permitted but will become subject to review by Research Management.
Your decision to buy or sell a security should be based upon your personal investment objectives and should be made only
after evaluating the stock's expected performance and risk.

VPEC’s Jul and Aug revenue delivered double digit YoY growth, or 
23% / 25% higher than our estimate, reflecting strong AI data center

revenues growth through Dec 2026, leading 3Q26 / 4Q26E revenues 
at 44% / 23% QoQ, and the product mix upgrade toward AI data 
center optical networking would continue to drive the GM 
expansion. VPEC’s July net margin up to 27% from 18% / 22% in 
3Q25 / 2Q26, reflecting the strong product mix upgrade. Maintain 
Buy with 12M TP raised to NT$793 (implied 69x 2027E PE vs. +61% 
NI YoY in 2027-28E). Read more: Global Optical Module TAM.

### Page 3

Earnings revision: We factor in VPEC’s Jul-Aug revenues and raise our 2026-28E net 
incomes by 12% / 18% / 30%, mainly on higher revenues and GMs. 2026-28E revenues 
are revised up by 7% / 14% / 25%, mainly on higher contribution from optoelectronics 
business, driven by the strong end demand of AI data center optical networking, better 
InP substrate supply, and VPEC’s customers’ expansion and product expansion from CW 
lasers to EML, along with specification upgrade. Our 2026-28E GMs are revised up on 
rising contribution from optoelectronics business, which carries a higher margin than

### Page 8

VPEC focuses on III-V compound semiconductor EPI wafer for microelectronics and 
optoelectronics devices based on InP and GaA substrate, and expands to EPI wafer for 
SiPh transceivers CW laser for data center applications. We expect strong momentum in 
VPEC growth driven by the SiPh ramp up in 2026E, microelectronics clients’ increasing 
demand, and its accumulated technology advantages on EPI wafer. We note that VPEC is 
currently trading lower than our TP implied 69x 2027E forward P/E, which is attractive, 
in our view.  
Price Target Risks and Methodology - VPEC 
Valuation: We adopt a discounted P/E method and apply a 22.2x target P/E on VPEC’s 
2029E EPS, discounting back to 2027E at a COE of 10.5% (beta 1.7x, risk free rate 1.6% 
and market risk premium at 5.1%), to derive our 12m TP of NT$793. Our target P/E is 
based on 0.4x PEG&M ratio derived from the average level of peers in the photonics 
supply chain. 
Key risk: Slower-than-expected SiPh business ramp up; weaker-than-expected 
microelectronics demand from smartphones clients; IDM offers EPI wafer in-house.

Accton Technology Corporation  | Asia Pacific
August Sales +4% MoM/+59%
YoY
In this report, we focus on Accton's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for share price movement.
Details:
• August sales were NT$40,873mn (+4% MoM/+59% YoY).
• QTD reached 66% of our 3Q26 estimate, at NT$120,883mn (+27% QoQ/
+66% YoY), and 70% of consensus, at NT$114,321mn (+20% QoQ/+57%
YoY).
Our view:
• We see 3Q26 revenue tracking in line with our estimates

• Our checks indicate that Accton has been negotiating with customers to let
them consign  those expensive components, which could weigh on its
revenue growth but should be positive to margins.
• Looking ahead, we expect the momentum to remain elevated into 2H26, as it
should benefit from broader-based migration to 800G network switches
from both existing and new customers, and the ramp of the new AI
accelerator model from its major customer should be in full swing.

• Stay OW with a PT of NT$3,500, based on 30x 2027 P/E.

Accton Technology Corporation (2345.TW)
Base case, P/E, which we believe better captures the company's earnings growth momentum.
We assign a target P/E of 30x to our 2027 EPS estimate, which we view as justified by an
operating profit CAGR of 48% for 2025-28, based on our estimates. This implies a PEG of
around 0.6, vs. its average of 0.7 over 2019-25, when the stock was trading at a P/E of 22x for

an operating profit CAGR of 32%.

E Ink Holdings Inc.  | Asia Pacific
August  Sales +20% MoM/+3%
Y oY
In this report, we focus on E Ink's monthly sales, which we
believe could be a catalyst for its share price.
Details:
• August sales were NT$3,446mn (+20% MoM/+3% YoY).
• QTD sales reached 63% of our 3Q26 revenue estimate of NT$9,985mn (-2%
QoQ/-4% YoY) and 62% of consensus at NT$10,213mn (flat QoQ/-2% YoY).
Our view:
• The solid rebound in the Aug monthly sales should alleviate the potential

risk of missing full-year guidance again (now at 10-15% YoY for 2026), in our
view, as  3Q26 revenue is tracking in line with our estimate for  a modest
decline QoQ.
• While the worst seems to be behind us and valuation is at a trough level of
12x 2027 P/E, we see no strong catalysts in the near term, despite our
positive long-term view on  e-paper demand across various applications.

Valuation Methodology and Risks
E Ink Holdings Inc. (8069.TWO)
Base case, 12x 2027e P/E. We believe this valuation methodology best captures E Ink's earn-
ings growth momentum. We view our target multiple of 12x as fair, considering our estimated
17% earnings CAGR for 2025-28. The implied PEG of 0.7x is largely in line with its typical level
in 2022-25, when the stock was trading at an average P/E of 22x one-year forward consensus

EPS with a 37% earnings CAGR.
Risks to Upside
n Firmer-than-expected ESL orders
n Stronger demand for e-readers and e-notes
n Better macro conditions
n Milder competition
n Brisker inventory digestion
Risks to Downside
n Softer-than-expected ESL orders
n Slower demand for e-readers and e-notes
n Macro headwinds
n Intensified competition
n More protracted inventory digestion

Date: 2026-09-09
Pages: 7
Status: ok

### Page 1

Taiwan Industrials

What’s new: Eternal Precision Mechanics (EPM) reported its August 2026 
revenue after market hours on 9 September 2026.

What’s the impact: August revenue beat expectations. EPM reported 
August 2026 revenue of TWD359.8m, up 95.7% MoM and 111.5% YoY. 
QTD revenue reached 88.4% of our previous 3Q26 forecast and 74.2% of 
the Bloomberg consensus. Given the faster-than-expected revenue 
recognition schedule and a sharp increase in recognised high-end 
equipment units, which should drive a more favourable product mix, we 
raise our 3Q26 revenue forecast by 33% to TWD972.7m, gross margin by 
3.1ppts to 48.5%, and EPS by 92% to TWD1.86.

Vacuum laminators are emerging as the next ABF bottleneck. Despite 
a partial conversion of backlog into revenue in August, EPM’s backlog 
continued to increase from TWD810m at end-July to TWD880m in early 
September. With lead times extending further to 36 months, vacuum 
laminators are emerging as the next bottleneck in the ABF capacity 
expansion cycle. Given the robust demand from ABF substrate makers, we 
see upside potential to EPM’s capacity expansion plans. On margins, we 
expect continued product-mix improvement and the full realisation of price 
increases to lift gross margin by 6.6ppts/1.3ppts YoY to 53.2%/54.5% in 
2027/28E, driving a 2026-28E EPS CAGR of 141%.

Moulding film adoption opens a new growth avenue. Traditional 
transfer and compression moulding typically use granular, powder, or liquid-
type compounds for encapsulation. During our visit to SEMICON, Japanese 
material suppliers Nagase (8012 JP, JPY1,150.5, Outperform [2]; covered 
by Masayuki Nagano) and Resonac (4004 JP, JPY16,070, Outperform [2]; 
covered by Hidemitsu Umebayashi) noted growing customer interest in 
moulding films. These offer better filling performance, better warpage 
control and higher flowability. This makes them increasingly suitable for 
advanced packaging applications such as panel level packaging and 
component-embedded substrates. EPM supplies moulding-film laminators 
for both applications, with revenue contribution expected to begin in 2027.

What we recommend: We lift our 2026-28E EPS by 22-26% to reflect the 
full realisation of price increases and improving product mix. We reaffirm 
our Buy (1) rating and raise our 12-month TP to TWD720 (from TWD600) 
based on an unchanged target PER of 40x, applied to our 1-year forward 
EPS forecast. Key downside risk: slower-than-expected substrate capex 
growth.

How we differ: We likely conduct a more comprehensive analysis than 
others on ABF industry demand and moulding film development.

9 September 2026

Vacuum laminators: the next ABF bottleneck

➢ 3Q26 QTD revenue ahead on higher high-end equipment recognition 
➢ Product mix and price hikes drive margins to new highs 
➢ Reaffirming Buy (1) rating; lifting 12M TP to TWD720

Eternal was established in 2022 through the spin-off of Eternal Material’s equipment division and its 
subsequent merger with Nikko-Materials, a wholly owned Japanese subsidiary. The company was listed 
in January 2026 and is the global leader in IC substrate vacuum laminators, serving all major substrate 
manufacturers worldwide.

innovation. Its equipment design emphasizes precision, extended lifecycle and reduced material
waste, aligning product development with resource efficiency and long-term environmental

### Page 3

Earnings revision: We factor in SZS Aug revenues, revise down 2026E earnings by 11%, 
revise up 2027E earnings by 1%, and keep 2028E earnings largely unchanged. We revise 
down 2026E revenues mainly on lower-than-expected Aug revenues, considering longer 
time for new projects to reflect on company’s revenues/ earnings. We revise up 2027 
earnings mainly on higher revenues, reflecting our positive view on SZS as the key 
beneficiary of rising foldable phones.

Valuation: We are Buy rated on SZS with a 12-month target price of NT$300 (vs. 
previously at NT$286) on lower earnings. Our TP is based on a 21.9x 2027E P/E (vs. 
previously at 21.0x), which is derived from the updated sector correlation of 2027E P/E 
vs. 2027E-28E EPS YoY (Exhibit 8), with re-rating supported by positive view on rising 
foldable phone penetration. The 21.9x 2027E P/E is also within SZS’s trading range since 
Aug 2019.

Price Target Risks and Methodology - SZS 
Valuation: We use a near-term P/E vs. EPS growth correlation to derive our target price 
for SZS, consistent with our Taiwan Technology coverage. Our target 2027E P/E multiple 
of 21.9x for SZS is based on the sector correlation of 2027E P/E vs. 2027-28E earnings 
growth. We thus derive our 12-month target price at NT$300. We are Buy rated. Key 
risks: Weaker-than-expected headset hinges demand; slower-than-expected foldable 
phone penetration; potential competition from more suppliers; soft market demand.

### Page 1

We hosted Repon’s management at our Asia Leaders Conference 2026 (Aug 31 - Sep 
2) in Hong Kong. Management remains positive on their servers rail kits business, 
driven by both general servers and AI servers, riding on the generative AI trend. The 
company’s positive tone echoes our positive view on AI servers supply chain, on 
which we raised our AI servers implied AI chips forecast by 14% / 22% / 14% in 
2026E-28E in June (report link) to +75% / 42% / 20% YoY in 2026E-28E, or 19m / 
27m / 32m in 2026E-28E. Capex estimates on leading US CSPs was also raised by 8% 
/ 27% / 25% in 2026E-28E to +76% / +35% / +8% YoY in 2026E-28E, or up to 
US$1.1tn by 2028E (report link). As we highlighted in our FII Chairman and Innolight 
Chairman visits takeaways, supply chain remains positive on rising AI investments in 
coming years, with spending across CSP , NeoCloud, Government, and Enterprise, and 
we are at an early stage of infrastructure spending and application development. 
End-customers are involved more in supply chain product development and capacity 
investment, also better reflecting real demand.  
Company profile: Repon (6584.TWO, not covered) is a leading rail kit supplier for AI 
servers, general servers, and home appliances. The company provides 2U rail kits for 
server clients, and has been gradually expanding its product line-up to 4U / 7U rail 
kits. As the early entrant of server rail kits, Repon has built deep partnerships with 
US CSP clients by offering customized services. 
Key Takeaways

1. General servers rail kits outlook: Management stated servers revenues 
contribution came down in 2Q26 vs. 1Q26 due to raw material shortage affecting 
customers’ procurement on rail kits for general servers; however, management sees 
their major CSP customer’s procurement recovering in 3Q26, and the next largest 
customer (also a leading US CSP) procurement is also recovering in September. The 
rail kits for next generation of general servers (powered by Intel’s Birch Stream 
platform) will also start shipment in 3Q26, supporting the revenues growth. 
2. AI servers rail kits outlook: Management remains positive and stated their rail

### Page 2

kits for the next generation AI server racks powered by NVIDIA is entering shipment in
late 3Q26, so is the rail kits for the next generation ASIC AI servers (air-cooling version)
for their major customer, and the rail kits for the liquid-cooling version should also start
shipment in 4Q26 with a majority ramp up in 1Q27. The rail kits for storage servers could
also show contribution in 1Q27, followed by rail kits for more ASIC AI servers, supporting

the growth ahead.

Industry View In-Line
We keep our 3Q26 iPhone build estimate unchanged at 54M units (+4% q/q, -2%
y/y). The slower y/y run rate reflects new model SKUs shifting to the premium
segment (18 Pro/Pro Max and iPhone Fold), while the iPhone 18 model is scheduled

for introduction in 1H27. We introduce our 4Q26 iPhone build estimate at 73M
units (+35% q/q, -4% y/y). Total new iPhone 18 model family units reached 71M
units (-21% y/y) in 2H26, with one less SKU launched compared to last year. We
expect 7M units of iPhone Duo builds in 2H26. A starting price of US$1,999 (relative
to expectations of US$2,300 or higher) appears favorable to builds, but there are
likely still some production issues that the supply chain is working on. This is why

the iPhone Duo is available to  the market only one month later, and we will
continue to monitor ramp-up progress for any upside or downside to builds. Our full
year iPhone build estimate is 235M units (+3% y/y).
Our 3Q26 iPad build forecast is unchanged at 12M units (-8% q/q, -14% y/y). We
attribute the 3Q sequential decline to some pull-forward demand in 1H and the
impact of rising prices. We introduce our 4Q iPad build forecast at 11M units (-8%

q/q, -21% y/y). Our full year iPad build estimate is 46.1M units (-15% y/y).

Analyst Stock Ratings
Overweight (O). The stock's total return is expected to exceed the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next
12-18 months.
Equal-weight (E). The stock's total return is expected to be in line with the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over

the next 12-18 months.
Not-Rated (NR). Currently the analyst does not have adequate conviction about the stock's total return relative to the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage
universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next 12-18 months.
Underweight (U). The stock's total return is expected to be below the average total return of the analyst's industry (or industry team's) coverage universe, on a risk-adjusted basis, over the next

12-18 months.
Unless otherwise specified, the time frame for price targets included in Morgan Stanley Research is 12 to 18 months.
Analyst Industry Views
Attractive (A): The analyst expects the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months to be attractive vs. the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated
below.
In-Line (I): The analyst expects the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months to be in line with the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below.

Cautious (C): The analyst views the performance of his or her industry coverage universe over the next 12-18 months with caution vs. the relevant broad market benchmark, as indicated below.
Benchmarks for each region are as follows: North America - S&P 500; Latin America - relevant MSCI country index or MSCI Latin America Index; Europe - MSCI Europe; Japan - TOPIX; Asia -

Investment Perspective
MLCC is early cycle in AI server & rack penetration
There is immense change underway for the MLCC industry with an investment narrative
that is changing as AI chips/server demand is increasingly driving MLCC scarcity.  AI is
shifting from semiconductors to MLCCs, creating a supply/demand mismatch in high-end
components. The high-end AI MLCC market is effectively a Japanese-Korean duopoly with
Murata and SEMCO together hold around 85% share. High-capacitance, low-ESL parts for

AI accelerators require hundreds to over a thousand dielectric layers with near-zero
defects and face strict customer qualification — the barrier preventing a repeat of 2017-
18, when shortages invited entry and the cycle self-corrected. AI platforms now compete
directly with consumer, automotive, and industrial applications for advanced materials,
heightening supply risk for MLCC traditional customers. We are still in the early innings,
and supply concerns are extending beyond near-term shortages to longer-term supply

security. As a result, we are seeing an increasing number of long-term supply agreements
being signed between suppliers and customers.
Exhibit 1: Sequencing the technology cycle – still early cycle for MLCC
Source:  Morgan Stanley Research estimates
Turning point in MLCC pricing
While Murata Mfg.’s CFO and Executive Deputy President Masanori Minamide stated in a
Sep 14 Nikkei interview that rising production loads for high-end products are making it

increasingly difficult to fully supply low-end products, and that the priority of defending
low-end market share has effectively declined, we believe the company’s fundamental
policy of not changing prices based solely on short-term supply-demand conditions
remains intact. That said, in our view, Murata has been gradually shifting its strategy
toward focusing more on its areas of strength and adopting pricing that better reflects the
need to cover large-scale capital investments, particularly in those core segments where it

enjoys a competitive advantage. We believe that Murata’s reluctance to enter into L TAs for
AI/data-center use value added MLCCs reflects its view that locking in prices today may
not be optimal, given the potential for MLCC pricing to rise in the future.
We expect sales growth to continue for small-sized, high-
capacity, high-value-added MLCCs for AI servers/DCs

### Page 3

M
Japan Insight
Morgan Stanley MUFG 3
MLCCs are a key business, accounting for 50% of sales at Murata, 46% at SEMCO, 19% at
Yageo, and 70% at Taiyo Yuden in 2025. We expect global MLCC shipment value to
expand at a CAGR of 20.3%, from $18.51bn in 2025 to $44.45bn in 2031. We believe
growth is set to accelerate from the 5.0% CAGR recorded in global MLCC shipment value
over the 13 years of 2012-25 because we expect continued growth in sales of small, high-

capacity, high-value-added MLCCs for AI servers/datacenters (DCs) from 2026. For AI
servers/DCs alone, we forecast MLCC shipment value to reach $23.33bn by 2031 (vs. our
previous estimate of $10.80bn), implying a 57.1% CAGR (vs. 38.1%).
Howard Kao (our Greater China Technology Hardware analyst) expects MLCC demand
volume for VR200 NVL72 racks to increase about 80% versus GB300 NVL72 racks, and
forecasts the number of MLCCs mounted in each Rubin NVL72 rack will jump to roughly

570,000 units from around 320,000 for GB300 NVL72 racks, with MLCC dollar content
per rack estimated to increase by 166%.　We expect the rapid expansion of the high-value-
added MLCC market for AI servers/DCs to be especially positive for  earnings at Murata (#1
market share in MLCCs for 2025 at 41%) and SEMCO (#2 at 23%).

Key roles of MLCCs in AI/DC
MLCCs play a role in locally stabilizing power supply (instantaneous current supply plus

noise removal) near semiconductors, such as GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. Since GPUs, CPUs,
and FPGAs repeatedly switch on and off on a nanosecond timescale, they demand large
currents instantaneously, and MLCCs meet this instantaneous current demand by
immediately discharging their stored charge. As semiconductor miniaturization advances,
circuit operating speed increases and drive voltage falls. As voltage decreases, even small
voltage fluctuations risk causing semiconductor malfunction, so even more stable power

supply voltage is required than before. Demand for capacitor capacitance is also increasing
in line with AI servers' rising computing power and power consumption, and because
board area and mountable space are limited, we expect demand for smaller, higher-
capacity MLCCs to persist.
Sharp dips vs. share price peaks provide re-entry opportunity
Year-to-date to Sep 11, share prices of the four companies had risen 127% for Murata,
449% for SEMCO, 141% for Yageo, and 160% for Taiyo Yuden. However, from their

respective June-July peaks, these have fallen 40% for Murata, 38% for SEMCO, 52% for

products for AI servers/DCs will continue to drive growth in MLCC demand not only in
2026 but also from 2027 onward, and that each company's earnings will stay on an
expansionary trend, we believe the conditions are now in place to consider re-entering

Earnings and share price risks
We expect capital expenditure on AI/DC to keep expanding and generational transitions to

continue in GPUs, sustaining growth in demand for small, high-capacity, high-value-added
MLCCs. Risks to the continuity of AI/DC capex expansion include: (1) rising risk from the
growing practice of hyperscalers and major semiconductor companies charging usage fees
in exchange for equity investments in AI development companies, conditional on the use
of their own cloud services or semiconductors; and (2) risk that AI/DC capex growth slows

due to bottlenecks, such as power infrastructure constraints. If the pace of AI/DC capex
growth slows, we cannot rule out that MLCC demand falls short of our base case outlook
for demand. Also, as shown in Exhibits Exhibit 8 Exhibit 8  and Exhibit 9 , during the IT
bubble around 2000, there was a strong correlation between the YoY change in Murata's
and Taiyo Yuden's monthly order intake and their market cap. Since order intake has risen
sharply since Jul-Sep 2025, we cannot ignore the possibility that YoY growth in order

intake will slow. On the other hand, MLCC demand continues to expand for high-value-
added products for AI/DC, and we expect the major MLCC makers' sales to grow along
with an improving product mix.

Role of MLCCs in AI servers
Capacitors, including multi-layer ceramic capacitors (MLCCs), function as a “dam” that
temporarily stores electricity, and are an essential electronic component for noise removal

and voltage stabilization in virtually all electronic circuits, including those used in
computers, smartphones, and automobiles. MLCCs play a role in locally stabilizing power
supply (instantaneous current supply plus noise removal) near semiconductors such as
GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. Since GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs repeatedly switch on and off on a
nanosecond timescale, they demand large currents instantaneously, and MLCCs meet this
instantaneous current demand by immediately discharging their stored charge. At the

same time, MLCCs bypass only the AC component (noise and fluctuating current), which
also serves to prevent noise from entering GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. MLCCs feature low
ESR (low resistance) and low ESL (low inductance), allowing them to track even

### Page 10

M
Japan Insight
10
nanosecond-level current fluctuations in semiconductors such as GPUs, CPUs, and FPGAs. 
MLCCs are often placed around components such as GPUs and ASICs that operate at low 
voltages of around 1.0V. As semiconductor miniaturization advances, circuit operating 
speed increases and drive voltage falls. As voltage decreases, even small voltage 
fluctuations risk causing semiconductor malfunction, requiring an even more stable power 
supply voltage than before. Demand for capacitor capacitance will also rise along with AI 
servers' improving computing power and increasing power consumption, and because 
board area and mountable space are limited, demand for smaller, higher-capacity MLCCs 
will likely continue. 
MLCC miniaturization and higher capacity to accelerate with 
VR200 NVL72
We assume that the space available for mounting MLCCs on VR200 NVL72 will not 
change significantly from the GB300 NVL72 rack, and that the transition from GB300 to 
VR200 will require installing higher-capacity MLCCs within the limited space of 
semiconductor ABF package substrates and AI accelerator boards, accelerating growth in 
demand for small-sized, high-capacity MLCCs. Murata has consistently been a leader in 
MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases, beginning mass production of 1005-size 1 F 
MLCCs in 2000 and 0402-size 1 F and 1005-size 22 F MLCCs in 2020. We expect 
demand for 1608-size 100 F, 1005-size 47 F, and 0603-size 10 F MLCCs to increase 
substantially with VR200 NVL72. We estimate that 1608-size 100 F MLCCs command a 
unit price 5-10x higher than 2012-size 100 F or 1608-size 47 F MLCCs, and we expect 
the shift to smaller, higher-capacity MLCCs accompanying the transition to VR200 NVL72 
to drive a substantial rise in ASP.

From a volume perspective, we estimate Cloud AI demand for 47µF+ MLCCs could 
increase from approximately 4 billion units in CY25 to 40B+ units by CY27: Such a 
rapid increase would represent a meaningful step-up in industry demand and could require 
substantial capacity reallocation or expansion among leading suppliers.
Based on our industry discussions, the market for high-capacitance MLCCs remains 
concentrated among a limited number of suppliers, primarily Japanese and Korean 
manufacturers, including Murata, Taiyo Yuden, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics (SEMCO). 
As demand from AI infrastructure accelerates, we believe capacity utilization for these 
products could tighten, raising the possibility of capacity crowding-out effects across 
other end markets and applications.

Materials development and production technology behind
MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases
In MLCCs, smaller sizes and higher capacities have mainly been achieved by thinning the
dielectric and electrode layers (layer thinning) and increasing the number of layers
stacked (multilayering). For high-capacity products for AI/DC, in addition to the layer
thinning and multilayering described above, efforts are accelerating to further miniaturize

and increase capacity by expanding the area of the dielectric and internal electrodes per
dielectric sheet. We believe MLCC miniaturization and capacity increases depend on: (1)
developing superior dielectric and electrode materials; (2) manufacturing highly uniform,
highly reliable slurry; (3) technology for precisely　stacking dielectric sheets; and (4)
technology for firing in a controlled atmosphere without oxidation. For high-capacity
products for AI/DC, we see the key factors as (1) materials development that increases the

crystallinity of dielectric materials while making them finer, in order to thin each dielectric
layer as much as possible (layer thinning), together with (2) manufacturing technology to
precisely stack the dielectric sheets.

Dielectric material manufacturing process
Dielectric materials are manufactured by adding a binder, solvent, and additives to barium
titanate (BaTiO3), which is produced from barium carbonate (B aCO3) and titanium oxide

(TiO2). Methods for manufacturing barium titanate are broadly divided into the solid-
phase method and the liquid-phase method. In the solid-phase method, barium carbonate
and titanium oxide are mixed and fired at high temperature, producing barium titanate
through a chemical reaction at the firing stage. In the liquid-phase method, barium
carbonate and titanium oxide are dissolved in a solution, reacted at the solution stage, and
fired at a relatively low temperature to produce the compound. Manufacturing methods

used in mass production via the liquid-phase method include the oxalate method and the
hydrothermal synthesis method. Barium titanate with small and uniform particle size is
key to smaller and higher-capacity MLCCs. In 2023, Murata established MF Materials, a
joint venture with Ishihara Sangyo and Ishihara Sangyo's wholly owned subsidiary Fuji
Titanium (with equity stakes of 20% for Murata, 10% for Ishihara Sangyo, and 70% for Fuji
Titanium). MF Materials produces barium titanate via the oxalate process and supplies it

to Murata Manufacturing.　MF Materials is constructing a new building adjacent to its head
office plant in Nobeoka, Miyazaki Prefecture, with operations scheduled to commence in
2027. TDK established a joint venture with Nippon Chemical Industrial in April 2026 called
TDK-NCI Advanced Materials (with equity stakes of 51% for TDK and 49% for Nippon
Chemical Industrial), with plans to accelerate development of the oxalate method barium
titanate.

Murata and SEMCO to benefit the most from growing
demand for high-value-added products for AI servers
We expect Murata and SEMCO, which supply small, high-capacity products stably and in
large volumes, to capture the greatest benefits from growing demand for small-sized,
high-capacity MLCCs used in AI servers and data centers. Murata has explained that AI/DC

MLCC sales accounted for 10-15% of its MLCC sales in F3/26 and are forecast to rise 100-
105% YoY in F3/27, accounting for 20-25% of MLCC sales. We estimate Murata's AI/DC
MLCC sales to rise roughly 120% YoY in F3/27 and about 100% YoY in F3/28, with AI/DC
MLCCs underpinning growth in the company's overall MLCC sales. Murata has stated that
it forecasts a 100-105% increase in AI/DC MLCC sales in F3/27, reflecting a roughly 40%
increase in volume and a roughly 50% rise in ASP, but we expect the increase in ASP to

exceed its forecast.
2025 MLCC market share was Murata 40.8%, Taiyo Yuden
11.3%
We estimate that global MLCC shipment value totaled $14.67bn in 2025 (up 10.3% YoY),
with shares of 40.8% for Murata, 22.5% for SEMCO, 11.3% for Taiyo Yuden, 6.9% for TDK,
and 5.4% for Yageo, and a combined 13.0% for all companies outside these top five. We
expect demand for high-value-added products for AI/DC to keep expanding from 2027,
with Murata and SEMCO continuing to gain market share.

What are the risks to Murata?
Risks for Murata include: (1) losing MLCC market share by failing to adequately supply
MLCCs for AI servers/DCs amid rapidly expanding demand. (2) Murata's products,
including MLCCs, are used not only in AI servers/DCs but across virtually all electronic
equipment, including automobiles, smartphones, and industrial machinery, making the
company sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and inventory cycles. (3) The company

has explained that a ¥1/$ appreciation of the yen would reduce operating profit by ¥4.5bn
per year, and the yen could appreciate beyond our assumed rate of ¥155/$, among other
factors.

Murata’s share price risk/reward: Even though we raise our earnings estimates for

Murata, we lower our DCF-based price target from ¥12,500 to ¥11,000, mainly reflecting
an increase in our DCF model’s risk-free rate from 2.60% to 3.0%. Murata's share price has
fallen 41% year-to-date from its June 22 peak, and we see 53% upside over the next 12-18
months, maintain our OW rating, and designate the stock as our Top Pick in Japan's
electronic components industry. The reasons are as follows: (1) We forecast the dollar-
based shipment value of MLCCs, where Murata held the top global share of 40% in 2025,

to expand at a CAGR of 21% through 2031, with Murata continuing to gradually gain
market share. (2) Demand for MLCCs used in AI servers/DCs is likely to continue
expanding, and demand for small, high-capacity, high-value-added products, which Murata
has brought to market ahead of competitors, should grow substantially. (3) Outside of
MLCCs, we look for demand to expand for small, high-value-added products, including
secondary batteries for DC BBUs, power modules for vertical power delivery in AI servers,

and RF modules for smartphones, and then expand even further as edge AI devices

become widespread. (4) In addition to earnings growth, we expect that management’s
proactive approach to shareholder returns, including share buybacks, will raise capital
efficiency and lift ROE.
Bull case ¥14,000, 95% projected upside
In our bull case, we assume higher sales of MLCCs for AI servers/data centers than in our
base case, for component sales of 7% higher than our base case, for OP of ¥560.3bn in
F3/27, ¥794bn in F3/28, and ¥1.515tn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF

assumptions are the same as for our base case. Bull case fair value corresponds to 58.2x of
fully-diluted F3/27 EPS of ¥240.4, 41.1x fully-diluted F3/28 EPS of ¥340.7, and 21.1x fully-
diluted F3/31 EPS of ¥664.0.
Bear case ¥3,500
Murata products are used in all kinds of different electronic devices, and they are easily
affected by the macro economy and inventory cycle. In our bear case, we assume slower
global economic growth rates and lower production of high-end consumer goods like

high-end smartphones than in our base case for OP of ¥314.6bn in F3/27, ¥330bn in F3/28,
and ¥362.4bn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF assumptions are the same as in
our base case. Here we look for ROE to increase from 8.8% in F3/26 to 9.3% in F3/27 and
9.4% in F3/28, above capital cost of 7.5%. With profit below the market consensus, we
assume the share price falls to a P/B of 2.4x.

SEMCO earnings forecasts
Shawn Kim
AI-driven MLCC growth and pricing to drive sharp earnings
acceleration in FY27, with continued growth in FY28
FY26-28 forecasts: We project SEMCO OP of W2.34tn in FY26 (+156% YoY), W5.70tn in
FY27 and W8.36tn in FY28, implying further growth of 144% and 47%, respectively. We
expect the earnings acceleration to be driven mainly by the Components (MLCC) and
Package Solution businesses, while the Optics business remains a relatively modest

contributor. In FY27, our projected OP of W5.70tn breaks down as Components W4.56tn,
Package Solution W943bn, and Optics W201bn, versus W1.67tn, W510bn, and W165bn,
respectively, in FY26. In FY28, we forecast Components OP rising further to W6.55tn,
Package Solution to W1.58tn, and Optics to W230bn. As such, we expect SEMCO's consol.
OP margin to grow from 8.1% in FY25 to 15.7% in FY26, 24.5% in FY27, and 25.9% in FY28.
We maintain the stock as our top pick within our S. Korea Technology coverage.

For Components, we expect profit growth to accelerate as AI-server demand drives both
strong MLCC volume growth and a structurally richer product mix. High-end AI MLCC
supply remains tight, with lead times exceeding 20 weeks, supply-chain inventories lean
following two years of destocking, and book-to-bill at the three high-end suppliers
reaching its highest level since the pandemic. Importantly, contract pricing has increasingly
been institutionalized through long-term agreements, while the high-end AI MLCC market

remains concentrated, with Murata and SEMCO together holding around 85% share.
Capacity additions are also unlikely to close the supply-demand gap quickly, as most
meaningful new capacity is scheduled for 2027 or later and suppliers are generally
targeting only around 10-15% annual output growth. We thus expect tighter supply-
demand, higher pricing, and a shift toward high-capacitance, low-ESL AI products to drive
Components OP margin from 21.4% in FY26 to 30.9% in FY27 and 30.1% in FY28.

Bull case W3,000,000
Our bull case assumes ABF opportunities from major US CSPs drive stronger content
growth, with future ASIC content & volume growth continuing to outpace our base-case
expectations. Customer diversification toward non-mobile customers should also reduce
earnings volatility and improve profitability. Our bull case, equivalent to 15x FY27e P/B,
reflects what we see as an unprecedented super-cycle in the underlying AI-related MLCC

and ABF markets.
Bear case W1,350,000
In our bear case, we assume slower content growth in MLCCs and substrates due to
greater competition and China's localization, together with prolonged consumer weakness
weighing on the Optics business. However, we still expect increasing AI exposure to
structurally lift SEMCO's MLCC and ABF ASPs, product mix and margins, given the
difficulty commodity suppliers face in penetrating the premium market. Our bear-case

value corresponds to 7x FY27e P/B. Key downside risks include a significant pullback in

Japan Insight
Morgan Stanley MUFG 25
Yageo earnings forecasts
Howard Kao
Tightening MLCC Narrative is Unchanged
We forecast CY26 revenue of approximately NT$183B, up 38% y/y, driven primarily by
stronger AI-related demand, with a more modest contribution from consumer
applications. This demand strength should support broad-based utilization improvement
across Yageo’s passive component portfolio. Pricing is also turning more favorable, with
distributor price increases implemented in 2Q26 and Yageo raising prices for direct

customers in 3Q26, as previously highlighted. The combination of higher utilization and
firmer pricing should drive meaningful operating leverage. We forecast gross margin
expanding to 39.3%, up 310bps y/y, and operating margin reaching 27.4%, up 500bps y/y,
supporting EPS of approximately NT$19.79.
Looking into CY27, we expect supply/demand conditions in the mid- and low-end markets
to tighten further, sustaining pricing momentum and driving an additional improvement in

utilization. We therefore forecast revenue of approximately NT$252B, up 38% y/y.
Continued operating leverage should lift gross margin to 43.2%, an increase of 390bps y/y,
and operating margin to 33.4%, up 600bps y/y, resulting in EPS of approximately NT$32.11.
Why has the stock been so volatile?
Yageo benefited from a sharp increase in MLCC pricing in 2Q26, driven by a temporary
spike in spot-market demand. In our view, ODM/EMS customers accelerated inventory

replenishment amid concerns that the ramp in high-end AI-server MLCC demand,
particularly alongside Nvidia’s Vera Rubin platform, could constrain supply of mid- and
low-end MLCCs. Under normal market conditions, these customers typically carry only 3-4
weeks of inventory. However, supply concerns prompted a rapid increase in inventory
coverage to approximately 4-6 months.
During this restocking phase, ODM/EMS customers sourced MLCCs from both
manufacturers, including Yageo, and distributors. The resulting demand surge drove a

sharp increase in spot/distributor pricing and also contributed to the stock’s strong
performance. However, the pricing move was largely driven by a one-off inventory build.
Once customers had secured sufficient inventory, purchasing activity normalized and spot
pricing began to soften. This, together with weaker broader market sentiment, led to a
pullback of ~50% from the stock’s peak of approximately NT$1,140.
At the current share price, however, we believe the risk-reward has become attractive. The

underlying fundamentals, and, importantly, our view of the MLCC upcycle, remain intact.
Our analysis indicates substantial incremental demand for high-end, high-capacitance
MLCCs of 47µF and above, which will require a meaningful increase in dedicated
production capacity. We expect this to drive further capacity conversion toward high-end
MLCCs, with the resulting crowding-out effect becoming more visible from late CY26 into
early CY27. This should progressively tighten supply in the mid- and low-end MLCC

market and provide renewed support for pricing.

Price Target Discussion and Valuation Methodology
We lower our 12-month price target to NT$1,050 (from NT$1,465): This reflects our
lower earnings estimates for CY26-28. Our price target is our base case value, derived
from our residual income valuation model. Similar to our analysis of other tech hardware
companies within our coverage, we think this methodology provides the most accurate

value of the firm by taking into account the cost of equity.
Our key assumptions are:
• Cost of equity of 7.8%:
° Risk-free rate of 1.0% (10-year Taiwanese government bond yield);
° Equity risk premium of 6.8%;
° Beta of 1.1;

• Medium-term growth rate of 12% (down from 16%);
• Terminal growth rate of 3%.
Our price target implies 33x 2027e P/E and 24x 2028e P/E. These are above its five-year
historical range of 8x to 18x, which we view as justified considering its longer-term
transformation story to become a global total solutions provider, moving from passive
into active components. In addition, compared to global passive component peers, we

believe Yageo stock remains undervalued with higher ROE and margins but lower P/E vs.
Japanese peers (which trade on an average at 40x+ P/E).
Our bull and bear case scenario values decrease by magnitudes similar to the change
to our base case value, to NT$1,490 and NT$480, respectively.

Taiyo Yuden share price risk/reward: We upgrade Taiyo Yuden from UW to EW, as we
believe its share price, having fallen 56.0% from its July 1 peak, has limited downside risk

and offers 6% upside over the next 12-18 months. We lower our DCF-based price target
from ¥12,500 to ¥10,500. This mainly reflects an increase in the DCF model’s risk-free
rate from 2.60% to 3.0%. We rate the stock EW rather than OW because: (1) In its core
MLCC business, we estimate Taiyo Yuden's MLCC market share was 11.3% in 2025, down
from 12.7% in 2020, and we think this downtrend continued into 2026, with its market
share shrinking to 10.7% in 1Q and 9.9% in 2Q. (2) We believe Taiyo Yuden is lagging

behind Murata (No. 1 share) and SEMCO (No. 2) in small, high-capacity MLCCs for AI
server accelerator boards, where demand is rapidly expanding. (3) We expect consensus
estimates for F3/28 onward to be revised down after 2Q results.
Bull case ¥14,000, 49% projected upside
In our bull case, F3/27 sales of MLCCs for AI servers/data centers are 7% higher than in our
base case, for OP of ¥56.5bn in F3/27, ¥85.5bn in F3/28, and ¥176.3bn in F3/31. Our forex

assumptions and DCF assumptions match our base case. Bull case fair value corresponds
to 50.7x our fully-diluted F3/27 EPS estimate of ¥276.1, 33.6x our fully-diluted F3/28 EPS
estimate of ¥417.0, and 15.9x our full-diluted F3/31 EPS estimate of ¥879.1.
Bear case ¥4,500
Taiyo Yuden’s care products (MLCCs and inductors) are used in all kinds of electronic
devices, and are easily affected by the macro economy and inventory cycle. In our bear
case, we assume slower global economic growth rates and lower production of high-end

consumer goods like high-end smartphones than in our base case, for OP of ¥39.2bn in
F3/27, ¥56.1bn in F3/28, and ¥65.8bn in F3/31. Our forex assumptions and DCF
assumptions are the same as in our base case. Here we look for ROE of 7.3% in F3/27 and
10.1% in F3/28, improving to a level above capital cost of 7.9%. With profit below market
expectations, we assume the share price falls to a P/B of 1.8x.

Global Research
First Read
Delta Electronics
Add to APAC Key Call Buy - Taiwan Summit
reaffirms the AI Power opportunity
Capturing a robust industry TAM as the leading server power supplier
Delta affirmed a stronger growth profile as AI infrastructure now is over 50% of sales.
Our bottom-up model from our APAC Focus (link) estimates a 69% CAGR to US$91.1bn
AI server power TAM from 2025-2030 even moderating 2028-30 for hyperscale cash

flow and grid power constraints. We see a strong 2027 driven by +65% YoY accelerator
die growth, Rubin's ~60% higher rack power and AMD's move to rack-scale systems.
400V/800V becomes a larger driver in 2028-29 as rising power density outgrows low-
voltage distribution. We believe Delta is key beneficiary with its  broad grid-to-chip
portfolio helping sustain its ~40% share of a rising TAM.
Near-term supply constraints bottoming from Aug and accelerating into Q4.

Supply constraints on Power ICs have tempered Q3 growth from +15-20% QoQ to +10-
12% QoQ but should grow in Sep and accelerate to double digit QoQ in Q426 and
above seasonal Q127 (UBS +3% QoQ) into new ASIC/GPU platform ramps and more
supply. Management expects shortages to persist for at least the next several quarters
with demand accelerating faster than supply and the supply-demand gap likely
widening before narrowing but price hikes rebounding OpMs.

HVDC Adoption Appears Increasingly Inevitable.
HVDC production and shipments have begun and should be modest in 2027 before
ramping sharper in the following 1-2 years. As rack power rises from 140kW on GB300
to nearly 250kW on VR200 and potentially higher on Rubin Ultra, management expects
space and efficiency constraints to shift power systems out of racks and into side-car or
centralized architectures. Delta sees HVDC as the logical solution for power-loss,

thermal, and density challenges, with higher-voltage architectures offering multiple-
times higher value per watt than current solutions. Delta sees three hyperscalers
evaluating 400V, two adopting it for NVIDIA racks initially before converging on 800V.
Reiterate Buy and PT NT$2,750
Delta's stock has pulled back 36% since May following push-outs to NVIDIA's
architecture slowing the dedicated power rack ramp-up and elevating supply
constraints, pulling it back to 22x/17x 2026-27 EPS. We now see better entry with sales

ramping in H226, spec upgrades to ASIC power racks and Rubin at 60% higher TDP over
Blackwell and margins holding better than feared. The company should leverage its
strong product line, R&D and field support to participate in the key power architecture
transitions in the coming years moving the power stack out of the rack and also
developing emerging nascent technologies including SST for facility level power
transformation and rectification and fuel cells licensing Ceres for medium-term

opportunity to supplement the power grid constraint with alternative energy.

Company Description
Delta Electronics provides computer switching power supply solutions, as well as video display
and electronics components, for computers, smartphones, telecom and industrial products.
Founded in 1971, the firm has production bases in Taiwan, China, Thailand and India. In

2023, its power electronics, infrastructure and automation segments contributed 62%, 25%
and 13% of revenue, respectively.
UBS EPS and Consensus EPS
The UBS EPS is an adjusted diluted EPS metric. It is calculated using the UBS analyst's
interpretation of earnings suitable for valuation purposes divided by the diluted number of
shares. This may differ to the way the consensus EPS metric has been calculated.
Valuation Method and Risk Statement
We base our price target on PE multiple valuation.

Delta's businesses include SPS and components for a variety of end-applications, video
displays and data networking subsystem and system products. Any changes in these end-
markets could affect our forecasts for Delta. Investment risk could increase/decrease on any
deviation from our expectations for end-market demand and competition.
Downside risks for Delta include: severe supply chain constraints; weaker-than-expected PC/
server demand; a slower-than-expected IA recovery; and a slower ramp of 5G in 2022.

from a direct investment in the underlying asset. UBS and its employees do not provide tax advice. Investors should consult their own tax advisor about their own tax situation

Global Research

Powertech T echnology
2026 T aiwan Summit: FOPLP to see more
revenue contribution from 2027F
FOPLP business supported by AMD and Broadcom
PTI attended our T aiwan Summit on Sep 14th. Management noted its  FOPLP capacity in
T aiwan will be at 6K substrate/month (3K in 2026 and add another 3K in 2027 with full
ramp in 2028) with panel substrate size of 510 mm x 515 mm. Management noted  most
of the capacity in T aiwan is allocated to AMD, which it will start from the  game-console

products and then target to enter server CPU. For the Broadcom business, PTI has
previously announced a JV with Broadcom in Singapore, where it will invest US$400mn
into the JV for 30% stake, after receiving regulatory approvals in Q426. The JV will focus
on Broadcom's next generation networking products and will help it to enter into optical
communication field.  It has not disclosed the total investment amount and planned
capacity for the Singapore JV fab, but we believe the planned capacity  could be 2-3x

versus its scale in T aiwan. The JV is expected to start mass production from 2028 and PTI
will be in charged of the fab operations. Nevertheless, PTI also acknowledges that
TSMC's CoPoS will not only lead to potential competition, but could  also have some
impact on the equipment supply schedule.
Memory-backed price hike should continue
PTI's August sales of NT$8,558mn was up 3.5% MoM and 24.5% YoY. QTD sales is
tracking to 69%/68% of UBSe/Street estimates of +5%/+6% QoQ. Management noted

its  back-end loading is already at 90% and it has been selective on customer programs
for better ASP products. Management also expects back-end ASP should continue to
increase, driven primarily by higher labor costs and rising component prices. At the same
time, the pressure to lower its ASPs and  share the profit from yield improvement has
eased. Relative to peers, PTI noted it has been less aggressive in implementing price
increases, but has increased the frequency of price negotiation with its customer. As a

result, its gross margin for  memory packaging and test should continue to trend higher
in the coming quarters.
Capex will remain elevated in 2026-27F
Management reiterate its 2026F capex guidance of NT$50bn and believes its capex in
2027F will remain elevated. It aims to use its internal cash flow and bank loans to
support the capex, and remains committed to keep its  dividend payout at ~60%. Full
year  revenue for 2026F is likely to surpass its prior peak in 2022 (i.e. NT$83.9bn),

although it believes  market expectation of NT$100bn in 2026E could be too stretched.
Valuation: Retain NEUTRAL with PT of NT$260
We retain NEUTRAL on PTI with PT of NT$260, based on 17x 2027 PE. We will continue
to monitor its progress on FOPLP/CPO and price improvement sustainability.

設備訂單供不應求，訂單能見度長達 9~12 月 
展望 3Q26 隨 AI/先進製程/封裝/記憶體投資帶動設備需求強勁，整體營收估
計 YoY>QoQ，其中製造服務 YoY、QoQ 皆為成長，維修受先進製程高稼動
率支撐，惟富蘭登受到上季認列航太專案高基期影響，預估 QoQ 下滑、
YoY 仍呈成長。自主開發受到升級改版產品導入先進製程，預估  QoQ、
YoY 皆為成長。因此，預估 3Q26 營收季增 5%、毛利率受到春武里廠稼動
率提升、檢測業務因客戶部份帶料而預期有所改善，費用率持平、推估 EPS 
6.32 元。目前訂單能見度至 9~12 個月，部份品項可看到 27 年底，預期營
收逐季往上，2026~27 年營收維持新高格局。 
看好檢測代工量能，毛利率亦有機會逐步改善 
2Q26 營收結構為半導體設備代工 85%、維修服務 14%、自主開發設備 1%，
其中來自設備代工分別季增 11%/年增 14%，隨先進製程推進及晶片結構複
雜度提升，帶動蝕刻、薄膜沉積與檢測等關鍵設備需求，以上三者營收佔比
>5 成。Repair 季增 37%/年增 125%，除了晶圓廠 UTR 維持高檔，主要成
長來自富蘭登 6 月認列航太專案。檢測設備營收年增 6 倍/佔比提升至 14%。
持續看好檢測代工動能，基於先進製程複雜度提升帶動高精度量測與檢測需
求增加，預估 2026~27 年檢測業務數量機會倍增，毛利率可望在 2H26 交易
模式改客戶自備高價料件，雖然造成營收貢獻減少，但有助毛利率提升。 
AI 帶動先進製程/HBM 需求強勁，新增泰國二期擴產計劃 
根據 SEMI 預估 2026 年 WFE 市場規模年增 23%，主要由 AI 帶動先進製程
需求，並已獲得客戶更長訂單需求，預計產能將為目前泰國廠一倍，預計
2H27 陸續投產。展望 2026~27 年動能來自 AI/HBM/先進製程設備需求維持
高檔，檢測設備代工、富蘭登營收貢獻擴大等。本中心預估 2026/27 年
EPS 21.83/27.44 元，分別下修 5%/上修 5%，主要基於訂單需求強勁及新
增二期擴產，主要受新廠費用、檢測毛利率波動而調整假設基礎。 
元大觀點

預估 3Q26 營收呈季增/年增，營收逐季新高。隨先進製程/封裝、HBM
等加速投資 WFE，訂單能見度至 27 年底。 
⧫  
展望 2026/27 年主力客戶展望佳/公司供應比提升及檢測、富蘭登訂單
需求強勁，搭配泰國擴產，營運可望優於產業平均。 
⧫  
預估 2026/27 年 EPS 21.83/27.44 元，維持買進，惟目標本益比降至

抑獲利成長空間，亦使評價有所調整。

產業概況  
先進製程與供應鏈在地化為大勢所趨 
自疫情後各國積極推動半導體供應鏈在地化，美國、歐洲、日本相繼祭出補貼以吸引先進製程及先
進封裝投資，使全球新廠與擴產計畫明顯增加，帶動設備與廠務族群自  2023 年起營收與市值持續
成長。 展望 2026 年，本中心預期設備與廠務族群仍將延續成長趨勢，主因包含 1)  AI 、HPC 需求
持續快速成長、先進製程產能加速放量 ; 2) 主要半導體製造商資本支出擴增、台積電美國建廠將於
2026 年加速，WFE (Wafer Fab Equipment) 將成長 9%。預估 2026 年主要晶圓廠資本支出達
1,792 億美元(YoY+37%)，其中台積電及海力士之資本支出年增分別為 51%/19%，美光同時也年
增 50%，反映 AI 帶動先進製程/HBM 相關設備需求強勁，將進一步推動廠務與設備需求加速成長。

帶動 HBM 需求強勁，Logic 除了 AI 相關投資以外，多數仍在消耗先前過剩產能為主，展望 2026
年景氣全面復甦、AI 持續擴大、新建廠效應，WFE 將進一步成長 9%，反映 AI 帶動先進製程/HBM
相關設備需求強勁，成熟製程方面，台積電也於 2026/7/16 表示海外成熟製程中以 PMIC 與 CMOS

2026 年半導體設備銷售延續復甦力道 隨著晶圓代工成長 
2026 年全球半導體設備總銷售額成長 16.2%達 1,450 億美元，預估 2027 年成長 7.6%，連續三年
創新高。預估晶圓廠設備銷售將於 2026/2027 年分別年成長 17.1%/7.7%，主要成長來自 AI 帶動
先進製程、HBM 需求強勁。 
觀察過去歷史循環，半導體設備營收年增率與晶圓代工廠營收年增率連動性高，且落後晶圓代工廠
約 2~3 季回升，並且半導體設備股價表現則與營收年增率呈現高度連動。

### Page 6

請參閱末頁之免責宣言。 台灣：半導體設備與耗材 2026 年 9 月 11 日 Foxsemicon 第6 頁，共 13頁  
獲利調整與股票評價  
維持買進評等、目標價降至 350 元 
元大最新預估京鼎 2026/27 年 EPS 分別為 21.83 /27.44 元，分別下修 5%/上修 5%，儘管公司來
自 AI 與 HPC 持續擴張，帶動先進邏輯、記憶體與先進封裝投資，設備訂單需求維持強勁，且動能
將延續至 2027 年。惟毛利率受到產品組合、泰國新廠初期營運成本影響，較預期低 0.5~1 個百分
點。目前訂單能見度長達 9~12 個月，部份訂單甚至到 27 年底。預估 3Q26 營收 QoQ、YoY 皆為
正成長，後續營收逐季攀升，2026 年營運表現可望優於 WFE 產業平均水準。2026 年營收主要假
設，雖然產業成長約 19~25% ，但部份設備拉貨 已提前至 2025 年 反應 ( 公司 25 年營收
YoY+26%>WFE YoY+ 12%)，26 年主要動能來自檢測新代工訂單、富蘭登完整年度營收貢獻，加
上泰國春武里 3Q26 投產，估計營收成長 21%，優於產業平均成長，毛利率估計較 25 年下滑 2 個
百分點，主要檢測設備業務為整機代工，毛利率偏低，另外，春武 里廠折舊估計加 1.6 億元及其他
初期營運成本等。27 年營收 YoY 成長由 7%提升至 15%，主要 2H27 新增泰國二期部份產能貢獻，
毛利率預期在檢測交易模式改變，估計較 26 年有所改善。根據 2026/27 年預估獲利換算本益比為
13/10 倍，落於歷史區間 7-15 倍的中下緣，略低於國內同業平均本益比約 18-22 倍、低於國外同業
30-45 倍。看好 2026~27 年營運持續創新高、中長期來自先進製程邏輯相關設備需求強勁及各國政
策建立自主供應鏈為重要動能。維持買進評等，惟短期股價反映毛利率低於預期而使評價面受影響，
因而目標本益比由 15 倍降至 13 倍， 2027 年 EPS 27.44 元，推得目標價 350 元。

公司簡介  
京鼎成立於 2001 年，專注於半導體、自動化及微污染防治設備之製造及銷售，前段晶圓製造以生產製程及檢測設備為主，
包含有化學機械研磨 (CMP)、薄膜沉積(PVD/CVD/ALD)、蝕刻(Etching)等設備製造，而備件則以真空製程元件及其他精密
機構件為主，包含濺鍍瞄準器、氣體整流器、CMP 研磨頭等。京鼎於 2002 年通過 AMAT 半導體設備製造商之合格供應商
認證，目前 AMAT 佔占公司營收約 8 成，其中京鼎在 CVD/Etch 代工營收佔比超過 5 成。

ESG 分析  
分別藉由「在 ESG 議題上的曝險」和「個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力」兩個面向來衡量公司於 ESG 上的表現。 
► ESG 總分： 京鼎整體的 ESG 風險評級屬於低風險，於 Sustainalytics 資料庫所覆蓋的公司中排名亦排行於靠前的位置，
但在設備代工行業中的公司中排名優於同業。 
► 在 ESG 議題上的曝險： 京鼎的整體曝險屬於低等水準，約等同於半導體設備行業的平均水準。公司較需要改善的 ESG 
議題包含人力資本、商業道德及資源使用等。 
► 個別公司在 ESG 議題上的執行力：京鼎在針對重大 ESG 議題的管理水準和執行力屬中等。京鼎於 ESG 相關揭露程度
高，顯示其對投資人及大眾的責任感極佳，雖說公司有針對重大 ESG 議題進行管控，但對於關鍵領域仍缺乏相關政策
及計畫。然而，目前京鼎尚未涉及任何 ESG 重大爭議。

貳、公 司 概 況

一. 公司簡介 
上品綜合工業股份有限公司（簡稱：上品；代號：4770）成立於
1981 年，總部位於台灣彰化，為全球少數具備從氟素樹脂原料加
工、半成品製造到內襯設備整合能力的一條龍供應商。公司核心
產品涵蓋氟素內襯設備、內襯管件及應用材料，廣泛應用於半導
體及電子級化學品產業的高純化學品儲存、輸送與製程系統，並
服務面板、石化等高腐蝕性化學環境應用領域。上品透過垂直整
合掌握關鍵原料與製程，能提供完整的客製化解決方案，確保產
品在耐腐蝕性、潔淨度及可靠性上的領先水準。公司於台灣彰濱
設有生產基地與研發中心，在中國浙江嘉興及美國亞利桑那均設
有百分之百持股子公司，結合當地業務與工程服務團隊，支援全
球客戶的建廠與設備需求。

截至 2026 年，半導體與電子化學品產業為上品營收主力，合計貢
獻超過八成，客戶涵蓋晶圓製造與先進化學品大廠。隨全球先進
製程擴產與電子級化學品本地化政策推進，公司積極參與台灣、
美國與中國多個新建廠案，並在高階氟素內襯產品市場形成與少
數日系廠商的寡佔格局。

二. 營運概況及展望 
產業概況 
氟素材料與設備產業屬於半導體與電子級化學品供應鏈中不可或
缺的基礎環節，其產品廣泛應用於高純化學品的儲存、輸送、製
程反應與廢液回收等系統，涵蓋化學儲槽、管線、內襯設備及運
輸槽車等。由於先進製程對化學品純度、製程穩定性與安全性的
要求日益嚴苛，氟素材料憑藉其優異的耐腐蝕性、化學惰性與低
金屬離子釋出特性，已成為電子級化學品系統的標準配置，對維
持半導體製程良率具有關鍵影響。近年來，隨著 3nm 、2nm 等先進
節點製程的推進，以及高純化學品用量的增加，氟素內襯與高潔
淨管路系統的市場需求持續成長，並高度仰賴具備客製化工程能
力與垂直整合生產的供應商。

競爭優勢 
上品在全球氟素材料與內襯設備市場的競爭優勢，核心來自其完
整的垂直整合能力與跨區域佈局。公司能從氟素樹脂原料加工、
半成品製造，到內襯設備組裝一次到位，並具備客製化設計與現
場工程整合的能力，能因應不同化學品特性與製程需求，提供高
純度、耐腐蝕且符合嚴格製程規範的系統解決方案。與少數日系
同業相比，上品在台灣半導體供應鏈的在地化程度與反應速度具
優勢，並透過美國與中國的子公司直接切入當地市場，縮短專案
溝通與交付時程。由於高階氟素設備屬於認證周期長、替代性低
的利基市場，進入門檻高，使現有供應商的市場地位相對穩固，
上品憑藉多年的專案經驗與穩定品質，已在半導體與電子化學品

製程擴產持續，對高階內襯與 ISO Tank 等設備需求穩定，為上品
的核心利基市場。整體而言，上品的競爭策略在於強化三大區域
的市場滲透率、持續提升在地工程支援能力，並鎖定高附加價值
產品線，藉此在全球建廠潮與化學品供應鏈升級浪潮中鞏固並擴
大領先地位。

未來展望 
上品將持續聚焦於高階氟素內襯設備與高純化學品儲運系統的技
術深化，並以半導體與電子化學品產業為成長核心。公司將延續
中國市場大型專案的出貨動能，並加速推進北美區 ISO Tank 等高
附加價值產品線的導入，藉由產品標準化與模組化設計，縮短交
付週期、提升客戶轉換意願。面對中國中階產品市場價格競爭激
烈的挑戰，上品將強化嘉興基地的在地製造與採購能力，以降低
成本並縮短專案導入時間，同時透過技術升級與高潔淨等級的產
品差異化，維持在高階市場的毛利水準與市場地位。

長期而言，上品將善用全球建廠潮與化學品供應鏈升級的契機，
持續鞏固在台灣半導體先進製程市場的優勢，並深化與系統整合
商及終端客戶的協作，將業務版圖從設備供應擴展至整體工程解
決方案提供者。此外，公司將逐步布局氟素材料的上游原料與製
程優化，以提升關鍵材料自主性與供應穩定性，降低國際局勢及
匯率波動帶來的營運風險。

叁、業 績 及 獲 利 預 估

QoQ 25.6%，YoY -5.2%，毛利率 35.6%較去年同期下降 1.74 個百分
點，主係部分出貨來自去年景氣相對疲弱時接下的訂單，議價空
間受限、毛利率偏低，隨著下半年漲價轉嫁與高毛利訂單陸續出
貨，預計毛利率將回升；營業利益 3.0 億元，QoQ 42.3%，YoY 
-15.1% ， 營益率 23.0% ； 稅後純益 2.5 億元 ， QoQ 23.4% ， YoY 13.0%，
純益率 19.1%，稅後 EPS 3.11 元。
